correctness.rationale: All 2835 nonempty matching faces of the explicit 12-vertex 24-edge graph are exhaustively enumerated; all 10816 Hasse covers were oriented and acyclicity verified. The explicit 1385-pair matching leaves exactly 1 critical vertex, 46 critical 3-cells, 18 critical 4-cells. Signed gradient recursion constructs full 46x18 Morse boundary, with F3 rank 17, rational rank 18 certified by determinant +3 of the specified 18x18 integer minor. Hence Smith factors 17 units and one 3. Because the 3-skeleton is a wedge of S3 and attaching maps are classified by degrees in pi3, the CW mapping cone is homotopy equivalent to 28 S3 wedge M(Z/3,3). Independent simplicial boundary ranks over F2,F3,F5 corroborate.

originality.rationale: Full primary matching-complex papers and the closest same-kind published finite graph classifications were inspected and compared by graph definition, ambient simplicial vertices and implication. Complete-graph torsion theorems, general line-graph connectivity bounds, and the outerplanar result do not imply this exact Chvátal graph homotopy type. The closest icosahedral torsion result has free rank 64 and different graph; the Grötzsch result is torsion-free. Residual risks of unindexed equivalents are explicitly recorded.
residual_risks: An equivalent Chvátal matching-complex calculation could exist in unindexed, privately circulated, or inaccessible literature.
The 2013 bounded-degree paper was checked at abstract/scope level only; it studies a different ambient bounded-degree complex, but its full details were not inspected.
Published calculation of the icosahedral matching complex establishes torsion in a different graph, so torsion itself is not claimed first discovered here.

value.rationale: A natural exact integral topological invariant of the canonical smallest 4-regular triangle-free 4-chromatic graph, showing both a free rank 28 and a nontrivial Moore summand, is significant beyond face counts and rational ranks. Its torsion contrasts with the previously classified torsion-free matching complex of the 11-vertex Grötzsch graph, another canonical triangle-free four-chromatic graph. This is a motivated complete finite homotopy classification, not a routine special case of a general published formula; no infinite-family or minimality claim is needed or made.
